facts.statement: IOMETE is a data lakehouse platform for AI and analytics
facts.quote: IOMETE is a state-of-the-art, fast, scalable, user-friendly Data Lakehouse Platform for AI and Analytics .

facts.statement: IOMETE is self-hosted software that runs in the customer's own infrastructure
facts.quote: IOMETE is a self-hosted data lakehouse: SQL, Spark jobs, streaming and notebooks on Apache Iceberg.

facts.statement: No customer data leaves the customer's infrastructure
facts.quote: The platform operates entirely within your infrastructure, ensuring that no data is sent outside of your organization.

facts.statement: IOMETE can be deployed on-premises, in the cloud, or hybrid
facts.quote: It offers flexibility and can be deployed anywhere – on-premises, in the cloud, or in a hybrid environment.

facts.statement: IOMETE can run fully air-gapped
facts.quote: It runs on your own Kubernetes, on-premises, in your cloud account or air-gapped.

facts.statement: The compute engine is Apache Spark
facts.quote: IOMETE utilizes Apache Spark, a widely adopted open-source data processing engine, known for its speed and versatility.

facts.statement: The lakehouse table format is Apache Iceberg
facts.quote: IOMETE uses the Apache Iceberg table format for reliable ACID transactions.

facts.statement: IOMETE runs on Kubernetes
facts.quote: IOMETE runs on Kubernetes, providing Compute Clusters that expose SQL endpoints for querying large-scale data.

facts.statement: The table format is open, so there is no format lock-in
facts.quote: Apache Iceberg is an open table format for huge analytic datasets.

facts.statement: Compute and storage are decoupled and scale independently
facts.quote: IOMETE utilizes a decoupled compute and storage architecture, which allows for the independent scaling of compute and storage.

facts.statement: Table data lives in S3-compatible object storage, separate from compute
facts.quote: Table data lives in S3-compatible object storage, separate from compute, so multiple clusters can share the same data without interfering with each other.

facts.statement: Iceberg tables support time travel queries to earlier snapshots
facts.quote: Time travel enables reproducible queries that use exactly the same table snapshot, or lets users easily examine changes

facts.statement: A query federation engine queries external sources without ETL
facts.quote: Query Federation Engine : Seamlessly query data from multiple sources, including relational and NoSQL databases, and flat files without the need for complex ETL pipelines.

facts.statement: There is a collaborative SQL editor with worksheets and dashboards
facts.quote: Collaborative SQL Editor : Write and edit SQL queries in real-time with multiple team members simultaneously.

facts.statement: Jupyter notebooks run on the platform for exploration and ML
facts.quote: Jupyter Containers : Interactive notebook environments for data exploration, ad-hoc queries, and ML development, running directly on the platform.

facts.statement: PySpark (and Scala) Spark jobs can be submitted and scheduled
facts.quote: You can submit Scala or PySpark jobs, schedule them with the Job Orchestrator , and monitor execution through the console.

facts.statement: Event Stream ingests JSON over HTTP into Iceberg tables without Kafka
facts.quote: Event Stream is a real-time event ingestion service that receives events and continuously makes them available in Apache Iceberg tables in near real time.

facts.statement: There is a native dbt adapter, dbt-iomete
facts.quote: The dbt-iomete adapter wires dbt into your IOMETE lakehouse with full Iceberg support, so you get versioned transformations on top of open table formats.

facts.statement: Airflow integration ships as the iomete-airflow-plugin
facts.quote: The complete source examples are available in the iomete-airflow-plugin repository .

facts.statement: Job Orchestrator scheduling is powered by Prefect
facts.quote: If you need scheduled, dependency-aware Spark job execution, the Job Orchestrator (powered by Prefect ) adds workflow scheduling:

facts.statement: Tableau connects over JDBC/ODBC, Spark Connect or Arrow Flight
facts.quote: You can connect BI and data science tools such as Tableau and Jupyter to IOMETE via JDBC/ODBC, Spark Connect, or Arrow Flight protocol.

facts.statement: Power BI has a dedicated IOMETE connector and Arrow Flight ODBC driver
facts.quote: The IOMETE Power BI connector connects Power BI to IOMETE through the IOMETE Arrow Flight SQL ODBC driver.

facts.statement: SSO supports SAML 2.0
facts.quote: SSO supports using either SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect (OIDC) .

facts.statement: SSO supports OpenID Connect (OIDC)
facts.quote: SSO supports using either SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect (OIDC) .

facts.statement: LDAP directory sync is supported
facts.quote: LDAP integration : connects to your existing directory service

facts.statement: Role-based access control is enforced through roles and resource bundles
facts.quote: They seamlessly integrate with existing data security rules to enforce role-based access control (RBAC).

facts.statement: Column-level data masking policies are supported
facts.quote: Ranger policies are managed through the Identity Service and control row-level filtering, column masking, and table-level permissions.

facts.statement: Row-level security filters limit which rows a user can see
facts.quote: Row-level filtering limits who can see certain rows in a database.

facts.statement: Apache Ranger policies are enforced on every data access request
facts.quote: Every data request passes through Apache Ranger policy enforcement, so access control stays consistent no matter how data is queried.

facts.statement: Table maintenance compacts small files, expires snapshots and removes orphan files
facts.quote: The Data Compaction Job cleans them up on a schedule.

facts.statement: Health checks run every 10 seconds and keep 48 hours of history
facts.quote: Checks run every 10 seconds, the service retains 48 hours of history, and status changes push to the console in real time.

facts.statement: Table maintenance enforces a 60-minute cooldown between runs on the same table
facts.quote: Cooldown between runs : after each successful run, the system enforces a 60-minute cooldown before the same table and operation can be picked up again.

facts.statement: JDBC/ODBC (HiveServer2) listens on port 10000
facts.quote: HiveServer2 (port 10000): JDBC /ODBC connections from BI tools, dbt , and other SQL clients

facts.statement: Spark Connect listens on port 15002
facts.quote: Spark Connect (port 15002): gRPC protocol for programmatic access

facts.statement: Arrow Flight listens on port 33333
facts.quote: Arrow Flight (port 33333): high-performance gRPC data transfer (when enabled)

facts.statement: Multi-cluster deployments are supported since version 3.16.x
facts.quote: Starting from version 3.16.x , IOMETE supports multi-cluster deployments.

facts.statement: Enterprise Edition supports multi-region deployment from one control plane
facts.quote: Multi-Region Support : Enterprise Edition features multi-region deployment for disaster recovery and high availability.

facts.statement: On-premises deployment is supported (rep claiming it is not)
facts.quote: Flexible Deployment : You can deploy IOMETE anywhere, whether it's on-premises, in the cloud, or in a hybrid environment, providing you with the flexibility to choose the environment that suits your needs.

facts.statement: SSO/SAML is supported (rep claiming there is no SSO)
facts.quote: SSO supports using either SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect (OIDC) .

facts.statement: Column masking exists (rep claiming only table-level security)
facts.quote: Ranger policies are managed through the Identity Service and control row-level filtering, column masking, and table-level permissions.

antifacts.wrong: says IOMETE is built on Delta Lake
antifacts.correction: IOMETE's lakehouse table format is Apache Iceberg, an open table format. Delta Lake is a different, Databricks-backed format and appears in the Enterprise Catalog only as planned support, not as the foundation of the platform.
antifacts.quote: IOMETE uses the Apache Iceberg table format for reliable ACID transactions.

antifacts.wrong: says IOMETE is a fully managed SaaS where the customer's data sits in IOMETE's cloud
antifacts.correction: IOMETE is self-hosted software that runs inside the customer's own Kubernetes and object storage; the docs state the platform operates entirely within your infrastructure and that no data is sent outside your organization.
antifacts.quote: The platform operates entirely within your infrastructure, ensuring that no data is sent outside of your organization.

antifacts.wrong: says the customer's data has to leave their network or that public internet access is required
antifacts.correction: IOMETE runs on your own Kubernetes, on-premises, in your cloud account or air-gapped, so nothing in the architecture requires sending data to IOMETE or reaching the public internet.
antifacts.quote: It runs on your own Kubernetes, on-premises, in your cloud account or air-gapped.

antifacts.wrong: says IOMETE is an open-source project and free
antifacts.correction: IOMETE is a commercial platform (Enterprise Edition, Helm chart iomete-data-plane-enterprise). What is open source is what it is built on: Apache Spark is an open-source engine and Iceberg an open table format. There is a free plan to start, but the platform itself is not an open-source project.
antifacts.quote: IOMETE utilizes Apache Spark, a widely adopted open-source data processing engine, known for its speed and versatility.

antifacts.wrong: says IOMETE is a BI/warehouse tool with no AI-ML story
antifacts.correction: IOMETE is positioned as a data lakehouse platform for AI and analytics, with Jupyter containers for ML development, Spark jobs and notebooks alongside the SQL/BI layer.
antifacts.quote: IOMETE is a state-of-the-art, fast, scalable, user-friendly Data Lakehouse Platform for AI and Analytics .

antifacts.wrong: says IOMETE only runs on AWS
antifacts.correction: IOMETE runs on any Kubernetes cluster: any cloud provider or on-premises data center, with S3, GCS, Azure Blob/ADLS, Ozone, Dell ECS and MinIO as storage options.
antifacts.quote: IOMETE runs on Kubernetes (any cloud provider or on-premises data center), stores data in object storage, and keeps metadata in PostgreSQL .

antifacts.wrong: says IOMETE locks customers into a proprietary storage format
antifacts.correction: Data is written as Apache Iceberg, an open table format with open metadata, so other engines can read the same tables; there is no proprietary file format in the lakehouse.
antifacts.quote: Apache Iceberg is an open table format for huge analytic datasets.

antifacts.correction: Event Stream ingests JSON over an HTTP API straight into Iceberg tables in near real time, explicitly so you do not have to manage Kafka or other message queues.
antifacts.quote: Event Stream is a real-time event ingestion service that receives events and continuously makes them available in Apache Iceberg tables in near real time.

antifacts.wrong: says IOMETE only has coarse table-level security
antifacts.correction: Apache Ranger policies are enforced on every data access request and cover row-level filtering, column masking and table-level permissions, plus tag-based policies.
antifacts.quote: Every data request passes through Apache Ranger policy enforcement, so access control stays consistent no matter how data is queried.

antifacts.correction: Enterprise Edition provides a control plane plus multi-data plane architecture for multi-region deployment and disaster recovery; multi-cluster setups have been supported since version 3.16.x.
antifacts.quote: IOMETE Enterprise Edition offers a control plane and multi-data plane architecture.

antifacts.wrong: says the backend database must be PostgreSQL
antifacts.correction: IOMETE supports either MySQL or PostgreSQL as its backend database.
antifacts.quote: For optimal functionality, IOMETE supports the use of either MySQL or PostgreSQL databases.
